title: Auditable per-request provenance ledger for multi-stage inference pipelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
We currently attribute token/input/output usage at multiple loosely-coupled points in the stack (edge proxy, request router, runtime workers, post-processing rerankers). This leads to discrepancies in customer invoices and difficulty investigating disputed charges — especially for hybrid flows that combine streaming chunks, synchronous fallbacks, and background reranking.

Goal:
Create a compact, append-only per-request provenance ledger that tracks authoritative consumption events across the whole inference path so we can: (1) produce a single canonical usage trace for each customer request, (2) reconcile differences between components, and (3) enable fast, auditable investigation and retroactive corrections.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: text and chat generation requests (streamed and non-streamed), model fallbacks (e.g., low-cost -> high-cost), prefix/KV cache hit indicators, postprocessing reranker/candidate expansions that consume tokens, and multipart uploads with attachments.
- Out of scope for this ticket: full multi-tenant ledger storage migration and long-term archival retention policy (follow-up). Encryption-at-rest and KMS integration beyond existing infra is not changed by this design.

Design overview (proposal):
1) Per-request Ledger Record (PLR): a small JSON line written at each meaningful stage containing: request_id, parent_request_id (if split), timestamp, stage (edge|router|worker|postproc|reranker), actor_id (service instance), token_delta_in, token_delta_out, effective_model, model_variant, cache_hit boolean, reason (fallback|retry|batch|manual), and an opaque signature (HMAC) to detect tampering during joins. Records are append-only and emitted synchronously where possible; best-effort emissions allowed for non-critical stages with a capture/retry loop.
2) Short-lived buffer: PLRs are buffered for 1 hour in the region-local ledger-queue (Kafka topic or SQS). A reconciler service consumes the stream and compacts per-request events into a canonical trace, producing the canonical usage row consumed by billing.
3) Semantic reconciliation: the reconciler applies deterministic rules to compute canonical token attribution:  - prefer worker-stage token counts over proxy estimates, - assign reranker costs to originating request if executed within 60s and same tenant, - attribute cached-prefix savings as negative token_delta_out on the worker stage so total still sums.
4) Audit API: provide an internal API to fetch the canonical trace and raw PLRs for any request_id. Support fuzzy search by customer, time range, and model.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Recording PLRs at every stage increases write volume but keeps records small (line-delimited) and enables exact replay for investigations.
- HMAC signing increases latency marginally but is required to ensure provenance across distributed components (prevents silent rewriting during aggregation).
- Using a reconciler centralizes complex logic so services can remain simple; adds a single complex component to own and test.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- Reconciler produces canonical usage rows with <0.01% mismatch against an independent accounting simulator over a 24h synthetic workload.
- Queryable audit API returns full PLR list and canonical trace within 5s for 99th percentile requests for the last 7 days.
- No more than 2 customer-disputed billing cases related to multi-stage attribution per month once deployed (baseline historically ~8).

Testing / QA plan:
- Unit tests for PLR schema evolution, HMAC verification, and deterministic reconciliation rules.
- End-to-end harness (local) that replays recorded traces from production sampling and validates reconciler output equals baseline ledger.
- Synthetic chaos runs: drop PLR emissions at random stages (simulate network loss) and verify reconciler correctness and retroactive repair path.
- Integration tests with streaming clients: ensure partial-chunk attributions and finalization semantics map into a single canonical trace.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag reconciler in staging, collect PLRs but do not switch billing consumers.
2) Run reconciliation in parallel (shadow) for 2 weeks, compare outputs to current billing rows, create discrepancy reports and tag offending flows.
3) Address top discrepancy classes (cache accounting, reranker attribution) and follow-up small fixes.
4) Gradually flip billing consumers to reconciler-ready rows for a subset of tenants (canary), monitor error budgets and invoice diff rate.

Monitoring and dashboards:
- Datadog: ledger-ingestion:records/sec, reconciler-latency:p99, reconciliation-discrepancy-rate, signed-plr-failures.
- Alert on reconciliation-discrepancy-rate > 0.1% over 1 hour.

Open questions / risks:
- How to handle long-running requests (>1hr) which may produce PLRs outside the short buffer TTL? Proposed temporary fix: stream PLRs directly to reconciler for these flows.
- Cost impact of increased PLR write volume for top tenants; need to model S3/Kafka egress.
- Edge-case: multi-tenant model sharing where reranker executes under different tenant credentials — must implement tenant provenance to avoid misbilling.

Next steps:
- Spike: implement PLR emission middleware for proxy and worker (2d) and a minimal reconciler consumer to compact traces (3d).
- Converge on HMAC key rotation policy with Security.
- Design Confluence doc for schema (link below) and schedule design review with Billing and Compliance.

2025-03-10 - Lina Chen (Billing): Reviewed reconciliation rules; requested explicit handling for preempted fallbacks and partial refunds. Adding requirement to surface raw PLRs in refund UI.

2025-03-14 - Marco Rivera: Implemented reconciler prototype and ran synthetic test harness against 100k generated traces. Discrepancy rate 0.07% — root causes: rounding differences and double-counted speculative decodes.
